title: Amendment to Real Estate Purchase Contract
summary: Change the price, closing date, repairs or other terms of a signed purchase contract.
useWhen: Buyer and seller agree to change a signed purchase contract, for example after inspection, appraisal or a financing delay.
watchOuts: Lenders must approve price and credit changes. Concessions above the loan program's limits can be disallowed.
Changing the closing date can affect rate locks, loan approval and the seller's next purchase.
Repair agreements should say who does the work, to what standard, by when, and whether licensed contractors and receipts are required.
If a licensee is involved, use the state-required amendment form where one exists.

variables.label: Repairs or credits
variables.help: What, by whom, standard, deadline, receipts. Or the amount of the credit.

variables.label: Other changes
variables.help: Any other changes to the contract.

sections.title: 1. Contract amended
sections.body: Amendment no. {{amendment_number}}, dated {{amendment_date}}, to the purchase contract dated {{contract_date}} between {{buyer_name}} ("Buyer") and {{seller_name}} ("Seller") for {{property_address}} (the "Contract").

sections.title: 2. Price
sections.body: The purchase price is changed to {{new_price}}.

sections.title: 3. Closing date
sections.body: The closing date is changed to {{new_closing}}. Other deadlines are not changed unless stated here.

sections.title: 4. Repairs and credits
sections.body:
{{repair_terms}}

Repairs will be completed in a workmanlike manner, by licensed contractors where the law requires, with permits where required, and receipts will be provided to Buyer before closing. Credits are subject to lender approval.

sections.title: 6. Everything else stays the same
sections.body: Except as changed by this amendment, the Contract remains in full effect. If this amendment and the Contract conflict, this amendment controls. Electronic signatures are valid.

sections.title: Signatures
sections.body:
By signing below, each party agrees to this document.

**Buyer** — {{buyer_name}}

[[sig:buyer]]

Printed name: [[name:buyer]]
Date: [[date:buyer]]

**Seller** — {{seller_name}}

[[sig:seller]]

Printed name: [[name:seller]]
Date: [[date:seller]]

disclaimer: This is a starting template from the Chucksi open contract library. It is not legal advice, and using it does not create an attorney-client relationship. Laws vary by state and change over time. Have a licensed attorney in your state review it before you sign. Real estate contracts carry state-specific disclosure, licensing, closing and recording rules. If a real estate licensee is involved, the licensee may be required to use state-promulgated or approved forms instead of this one (for example in Texas and Colorado). Deeds, mortgages and deeds of trust usually must be notarized and recorded; an electronic signature on this document does not record anything.
